title: PBR: Cook-Torrance BRDF Deep Dive
subtitle: From Theory to Real-Time Implementation
excerpt: A comprehensive breakdown of the Cook-Torrance specular BRDF, GGX distribution, and Fresnel equations for physically-based rendering.

sections.content: Physically Based Rendering (PBR) has become the industry standard for real-time graphics. At its core is the Bidirectional Reflectance Distribution Function (BRDF), which mathematically describes how light interacts with surfaces.
All PBR implementations are approximations of the rendering equation. The BRDF is the key term that determines surface appearance based on incoming and outgoing light directions.

sections.title: GGX Normal Distribution Function

sections.content: The Fresnel effect describes how reflectivity increases at grazing angles. Schlick's approximation provides an efficient polynomial fit.

sections.title: Fresnel-Schlick

sections.content: The geometry term accounts for self-shadowing from microfacets. We use Smith's method with GGX for both view and light directions.

sections.title: Smith-GGX Geometry Function

sections.content: For Image-Based Lighting (IBL), use k = (roughness^2) / 2 instead of the direct lighting remapping.

sections.title: Cook-Torrance Specular BRDF

items: D (Distribution): Probability of microfacets aligned with half-vector
F (Fresnel): Ratio of reflected vs refracted light
G (Geometry): Self-shadowing attenuation from rough surfaces
